request.spec:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transfer undo is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**Behaviour:** each person row now has an "Undo transfer" button. A steward can use it on the sheet a person was transferred to, on the same sheet-today the person arrived. The person goes back to the sheet they came from through the existing transfer code, so the transfer rules, refusals and audit lines are exactly the same. After that, this sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> to=<origin>`, followed by a `TOTALS` line. The spec expects that `TOTALS` line even though the transfer back already wrote one.

The undo is refused, with the error on the row and nothing written, if:
- the user isn't a steward,
- the person didn't arrive by transfer, or
- it's a later day than the one they arrived.

**Changes:**
- **Database:** new migration `V96__person_arrived_on.sql` adds an `arrived_on` column to `person`. A transfer sets it to the receiving sheet's today.
- **Server:** `PersonTransferService.undoTransfer` does the checks and the transfer back. `PersonController` exposes it as `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{id}/transfer-undo`.
- **Front end:** the `person-transfer-undo` button in `features/people/people.ts` and an `undoTransfer` call in `core/people.ts`. After a successful undo the sheet is re-read.

**Limits:**
- People transferred before this change have no arrival date, so their transfers can't be undone.
- When a transfer merges the person into someone already on the other sheet, there's no row left that arrived by transfer, so there's nothing to undo.
- An undone person ends up back on their old sheet as a new arrival from this one. That means a steward there could undo the undo on that same day.
